It makes a copy of an ID photo that is safer to share. Sensitive details such as the first 8 digits of your Aadhaar number and the QR code are covered with solid black boxes. The copy is stamped with who it is for and the date, and saved as a new image without hidden information like location or phone model. Your original photo is not kept.
The QR code on an Aadhaar card or letter holds your full details, including your photo, and many QR reader apps can show them. Covering the number but not the QR code leaves all of that readable.
When do I need to share my full Aadhaar number?

Some regulated services, such as certain bank or SIM card KYC checks, may ask for the full number. Follow the instructions of the organisation asking. Many others accept a masked Aadhaar that shows only the last 4 digits. If you do need the full number, open Detected fields in the editor and switch off the Aadhaar number. The watermark still shows who the copy is for.

No. Someone with photo-editing skills could try to remove it. The text is repeated across the whole image and over the black boxes to make that harder. Its job is to discourage misuse and to show who a leaked copy was given to.
How can I check that SafeCopy is offline?

SafeCopy does not ask for the internet permission, so Android doesn\'t let it use the network. On Google Play, open SafeCopy\'s page and look at About this app, then App permissions: there is no network access entry. You can also turn on airplane mode, and SafeCopy works the same. Technical users can inspect the APK with Android Studio\'s APK Analyzer.
How do I use it from WhatsApp?
When someone asks for your ID, open the photo, tap Share and choose SafeCopy instead of sending it to the chat. Make the safe copy, then tap Share and pick WhatsApp to send it.
Does SafeCopy make a document valid or invalid?
No. It doesn\'t change whether a document is accepted, and an organisation may still ask for the full, unmasked document. SafeCopy is not affiliated with UIDAI or the Income Tax Department.
